previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, diastolic heart failure, and a history of mitral valve replacement was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure with severe bilateral leg edema and shortness of breath. She had been nonadherent with her torsemide, leading to fluid overload. She was treated with aggressive IV diuresis, transitioned to high-dose oral torsemide and metolazone, and managed for hyperkalemia and uncontrolled diabetes. A right heart catheterization confirmed elevated biventricular filling pressures. She received a course of antibiotics for suspected HCAP, which resolved. Her left heel ulcer was stable, and no active infection was found. Despite improvement, she chose to leave against medical advice due to a recent hypoglycemic episode, after demonstrating understanding of the risks. She was discharged home with services on increased diuretics, warfarin, insulin, and multiple comorbid medications, with close follow-up arranged.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft

resolved. While on the floor, she was maintained on NPH and ISS

relative to her dry weight of 72 kg. She was transferred to

#Complicated UTI: On admission, she was noted to have a UA

g PO/NG EVERY OTHER DAY Duration: 3 Doses (___). 
Fosfomycin sensitivities were pending at time of discharge, with 
plans to follow up the sensitivities. Risks of nephrotoxicity 
and ototoxicity associated with tobramycin were weighed against 
the lower risk that her organism is resistant to fosfomycin. She 
has been afebrile without leukocytosis and there is no evidence 
of pyelonephritis; fosfomycin is an excellent choice for 
cystitis from a resistant organism.  She will also continue PO 
vanc (see below cdiff) while on fosfomycin.

# Mid-thoracic pain/weakness: generalized weakness, but no focal

on ___. Foci of hypodensity in the subcortical, deep, and
periventricular white matter of the cerebral hemispheres have progressed
